claims.text: A machine-learning approach using atomic-scale features can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The machine-learning approach will outperform traditional empirical models.
The model will be trained using atomic-scale features and thermal-conductivity data.
The training dataset will contain diverse known high-entropy alloys and their phonon thermal conductivities measured under controlled temperature conditions.
Atomic arrangement, bonding characteristics, and elemental composition are relevant atomic-scale predictors of phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys.
Machine learning can capture complex relationships between atomic-scale features and thermal conductivity.
Capturing these complex relationships produces better predictions than models based on simpler correlations.
Existing empirical models use simpler correlations between composition and thermal conductivity.
The approach will identify high-entropy alloys with phonon thermal conductivity below 1 W/m·K.
The approach will improve prediction accuracy by 20% relative to existing empirical models.
The approach is applicable specifically to high-entropy alloys.
The approach may not generalize to material classes or systems governed by different thermal-transport mechanisms.
The magnitude of improvement may depend on the dataset and model features.
